name: Citicoline + Piracetam
meta: Citicoline (CDP-Choline): Neuroprotective / nootropic; Piracetam: Nootropic (cyclic GABA derivative)
Schedule H – prescription only; Piracetam: Schedule H – prescription only
sections: White crystalline powder (sodium salt), freely soluble in water.
White crystalline powder, freely soluble in water; melting point 152 °C.

Citicoline (CDP-Choline): Citicoline occurs naturally in all cells as an intermediate of phosphatidylcholine synthesis; it is a prescription drug in many European and Asian countries and a supplement elsewhere. The ICTUS trial (2012) did not show benefit in moderate-to-severe acute ischaemic stroke. First approval/introduction: Developed in Japan and Spain in the 1970s (Ferrer Internacional). Piracetam: The first 'nootropic'; Giurgea coined the term in 1972. Approved in many European and Asian countries but not in the USA. First approval/introduction: Synthesised 1964 by Corneliu E. Giurgea at UCB; marketed 1971.
Citicoline supports phospholipid membrane repair and acetylcholine synthesis; piracetam enhances neuronal membrane fluidity and microcirculation. Complementary neuroprotective and nootropic actions.

Citicoline (CDP-Choline) Intermediate in phosphatidylcholine synthesis; supports neuronal membrane repair, increases acetylcholine and dopamine availability, reduces free-fatty-acid release and free-radical damage after ischaemic or traumatic brain injury. Receptor / target profile: Intermediate in phosphatidylcholine synthesis; increases acetylcholine, dopamine and norepinephrine levels, decreases glutamate and free fatty acids, and preserves membrane phospholipids.

Piracetam Enhances neuronal membrane fluidity and cholinergic/glutamatergic neurotransmission; improves cerebral microcirculation by reducing platelet aggregation and red-cell rigidity. Used for cortical myoclonus and cognitive impairment. Receptor / target profile: Mechanism not fully defined: increases membrane fluidity, modulates AMPA and cholinergic transmission, reduces erythrocyte adhesion and platelet aggregation.
Hydrolysed in gut wall and liver to choline and cytidine (uridine), which cross the blood–brain barrier and resynthesise CDP-choline
Summary: Oral bioavailability >90%; hydrolysed to choline and cytidine, which cross the blood–brain barrier and are resynthesised. Eliminated via respiration (CO2) and urine.
Summary: Rapid, complete absorption; Tmax ~1 h. Not protein bound; not metabolised. Half-life ~5 h. Excreted unchanged in urine – adjust in renal impairment.

Citicoline (CDP-Choline): Low toxicity; supportive care. Piracetam: Low toxicity; bloody diarrhoea and abdominal pain reported with very large doses. Supportive care; haemodialysis removes it.
Evidence derives from component trials; no large randomised trials of the fixed combination.
